attacks.claim: No delta sync is planned between the MailPoet subscriber snapshot and cutover. The final MailPoet send is Thursday of week 3 and cutover is the following Tuesday, so unsubscribes, bounces and complaints from that send can arrive after the export. If the production import uses an earlier snapshot, Ghost could re-mail opted-out readers, which is a compliance and trust failure.
attacks.evidence: "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed (never as active), so nobody who opted out is re-mailed." / ABSENT: timing of production import relative to the week 3 final send, or a delta re-export before cutover

attacks.claim: Rollback only re-imports new Ghost signups into MailPoet. Unsubscribes, bounces and complaints recorded in Ghost or Mailgun after cutover have no reverse path, and no field mapping is given for suppression status. Re-enabling MailPoet could re-mail readers who opted out during the Ghost window. Post-cutover paid-member changes are also not covered.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet"

attacks.claim: The first-send deliverability gate is weak. Mailgun warm-up is a single week 2 line item with no volume ramp, yet the first Ghost send in week 4 goes to a cold domain and the remainder follows 2 hours after the 2,000 seed. Two hours is too short to surface complaint signals on a seed of about 2 complaints at 0.1%. The remainder also appears to send automatically, with no named human go/no-go owner or abort path.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" / "the remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%"

attacks.claim: The plan has no monitoring, alerting or send-day on-call owner on the single VPS that runs the web app and MySQL. The 'zero send-day outages' goal therefore cannot be detected or acted on. Backups are nightly only, and a full DB-dump restore is not rehearsed, only an export restore.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)" / ABSENT: alerting, on-call for send days, DB restore drill

attacks.claim: Consent provenance is migrated only 'where recorded'. The plan does not say how subscribers with no recorded consent are handled, or what retention rule applies to the IP-linked consent records and the old WordPress instance kept for 30 days.
The 37 mismatched paid members are to be fixed by hand with no named owner, deadline or verification step. The work lands in the same week as the Stripe dry run, so there is no buffer before cutover.
attacks.evidence: "37 members with mismatched emails were identified in a dry run and will be resolved by hand before cutover."
